licensing: SYNTHETIC ONLY. Every vector below is a generated byte pattern -- there is not one byte of Commodore boot1/boot2/kernel content in this file, and none may ever be added. Real artifacts appear in contracts/bootchain-v1.json as sha256 + expected sum only; a hash is not the content.

encoding.note: Vectors are described GENERATIVELY, not stored as bytes, so a 16 MiB boundary case costs one JSON line instead of 16 MiB in git. Every generator is deterministic; two independent implementations building the same vector must get the same bytes.

generators.repeat: one byte value repeated count times. {"kind":"repeat","byte":255,"count":256}
generators.range: the bytes start, start+1, ... start+count-1, each masked to 8 bits. {"kind":"range","start":0,"count":256}
generators.cycle: the pattern array repeated until count bytes are produced. {"kind":"cycle","pattern":[0,255],"count":1024}

expected_field: sum -- the svr4-sum result, an integer in [0, 0xFFFF]

vectors.name: empty
vectors.why: degenerate case; an implementation that seeds its accumulator wrong fails here

vectors.name: single-ff
vectors.why: bytes must be summed UNSIGNED; a signed-char implementation returns -1/65535 here

vectors.name: zeros-4096
vectors.why: length must not influence the result when every byte is zero

vectors.name: iblk-magic
vectors.why: the literal IBLK ident field; a small realistic-looking buffer

vectors.name: bytes-0-255
vectors.why: every possible byte value exactly once; catches masking errors mid-range

vectors.name: alt-00ff-1024
vectors.why: just under the first fold boundary

vectors.name: ff-256
vectors.why: 0xFF00 -- still inside 16 bits, no fold effect yet

vectors.name: ff-257
vectors.why: EXACTLY 0xFFFF -- the fold boundary, straddled from below

vectors.name: ff-258
vectors.why: 0x1017E -- the first buffer that actually CARRIES into the fold. An implementation that forgets to fold returns 65790 here

vectors.name: ff-16843009
vectors.why: byte total is EXACTLY 0xFFFFFFFF. First fold gives 0x1FFFE, which is > 16 bits -- so this vector is what proves the SECOND fold is performed. A single-fold implementation returns 0x1FFFE (131070)
vectors.size_note: 16 MiB when generated; generative on purpose, never stored

vectors.name: ff-16843010
vectors.why: THE 32-BIT WRAP VECTOR. Byte total is 0x1000000FE = 2**32 + 254, which wraps to 254 in the C `unsigned long` accumulator. An implementation using arbitrary-precision integers without a modulo-2**32 step returns 255 here and is wrong. This is the single most valuable vector in the file: every other vector passes on both the correct and the unwrapped implementation
vectors.size_note: 16 MiB when generated; generative on purpose, never stored
